question.text: Saraswati Structured Credit AIF is originating a Securitized Debt Instrument (SDI) where the target company — a drone manufacturer — takes capital equipment on lease from an SPV funded by the AIF. Under SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations, who bears the primary responsibility for due diligence on the lessee (target) company?

answer.text: The originator / sponsor of the SDI
The stock exchange where the SDI is listed
The credit rating agency rating the SDI
The trustee of the AIF holding the SDI

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Series XIX-C page 259, the originator or sponsor of the SDI is responsible for conducting due diligence on the target company that takes the assets on lease. This includes management reference checks, financial red flags, key contracts, lenders, defaults, compliance issues, and litigations. The Trap: The stock exchange, the credit rating agency, and the AIF trustee are not assigned the primary SDI due-diligence responsibility on page 259; that duty sits with the originator/sponsor. Note: Tie the answer specifically to the sponsor/originator due-diligence checklist set out on page 259.
